STOICHEIA / EUCLID II.14 / A SAVED CONSTRUCTION

A square, with nothing added.

Given rectangle: 9 by 4 drawing units. Area: 36 square units. Constructed side: approximately 6 units. The half-sum 6.5 makes its square 6.25 square units too large.

Open these settings in the workshop · Save the exact measurement table

Equal area and equal perimeter are different conditions
FigureSide(s)AreaPerimeter
Given rectangle9 × 4 u36 u²26 u
Square on ΕΘ6 u36 u²24 u
Square on the half-sum6.5 u42.25 u²26 u

The extra area in the average

The two pieces have areas 26 and 10 square units. A square with the rectangle's half-sum as its side has the same perimeter, but is larger in area unless the sides are equal.

Subtract the common square

II.5: rectangle + square on ΗΕ = square on ΗΖ. Equal radii make the latter the square on ΗΘ. I.47: square on ΕΘ + square on ΗΕ = square on ΗΘ. Subtract the common 6.25 u² square. The remaining rectangle and constructed square are equal in area.

The rectangle's right angle makes ΗΕΘ a right triangle. I.46 supplies the final square on the constructed side.

The complete argument

Greek: Heiberg's 1883 edition. Latin: his nineteenth-century translation, not an ancient Latin text. English and reading divisions are new. The complete proposition includes a preliminary conversion of a general rectilinear figure by I.45. This workshop implements its rectangle case.

1. A square equal to a figure

Τῷ δοθέντι εὐθυγράμμῳ ἴσον τετράγωνον συστήσασθαι. Ἔστω τὸ δοθὲν εὐθύγραμμον τὸ Α· δεῖ δὴ τῷ Α εὐθυγράμμῳ ἴσον τετράγωνον συστήσασθαι.

Quadratum datae figurae rectilineae aequale construere. Sit data figura rectilinea Α. oportet igitur figurae rectilineae Α aequale quadratum construere.

To construct a square equal to the given rectilinear figure. Let Α be the given rectilinear figure. We must therefore construct a square equal to the rectilinear figure Α.

ἴσον · aequale — equal — here, in area. ἴσον agrees with τετράγωνον, ‘square’. The dative τῷ … εὐθυγράμμῳ names what it is equal to. Equal area does not require equal sides or the same shape. Α names a whole figure, not a point. Our workshop starts with a rectangle; the proposition's opening claim is more general.

Printed pages 160, 161.

2. An earlier construction supplies a rectangle

Συνεστάτω γὰρ τῷ Α εὐθυγράμμῳ ἴσον παραλληλόγραμμον ὀρθογώνιον τὸ ΒΔ·

construatur enim figurae rectilineae Α aequale parallelogrammum rectangulum ΒΔ.

For let the rectangular parallelogram ΒΔ be constructed equal to the rectilinear figure Α.

ὀρθογώνιον · rectangulum — right-angled. A parallelogram alone need not be a rectangle: ὀρθογώνιον adds the right-angle condition. Heiberg's Latin cites I.45 here. That earlier construction converts a rectilinear figure to an equal-area parallelogram at a specified angle. It is a prerequisite, not an operation carried out by this rectangle workshop. ΒΔ names the rectangle by opposite corners.

Printed pages 160, 161.

3. Already a square? Stop here

εἰ μὲν οὖν ἴση ἐστὶν ἡ ΒΕ τῇ ΕΔ, γεγονὸς ἂν εἴη τὸ ἐπιταχθέν. συνέσταται γὰρ τῷ Α εὐθυγράμμῳ ἴσον τετράγωνον τὸ ΒΔ· εἰ δὲ οὔ, μία τῶν ΒΕ, ΕΔ μείζων ἐστίν.

si igitur ΒΕ = ΕΔ, effectum erit, quod propositum erat. constructum enim est quadratum ΒΔ datae figurae rectilineae Α aequale. sin minus, alterutra rectarum ΒΕ, ΕΔ maior est.

If ΒΕ equals ΕΔ, what was required would already be done: the square ΒΔ has been constructed equal to the rectilinear figure Α. If not, one of ΒΕ and ΕΔ is greater.

εἰ μὲν … εἰ δὲ οὔ — if … but if not. The two conditions divide the argument. γεγονὸς ἂν εἴη uses a perfect participle with a potential optative: the task would stand accomplished. The semicircle is unnecessary when the given rectangle is a square. Choosing the larger side as ΒΕ fixes the orientation of the remaining construction.

Printed pages 160, 161.

4. Copy a side and bisect the whole

ἔστω μείζων ἡ ΒΕ, καὶ ἐκβεβλήσθω ἐπὶ τὸ Ζ, καὶ κείσθω τῇ ΕΔ ἴση ἡ ΕΖ, καὶ τετμήσθω ἡ ΒΖ δίχα κατὰ τὸ Η,

sit maior ΒΕ, et producatur ad Ζ, et ponatur ΕΖ = ΕΔ, et ΒΖ in Η in duas partes aequales secetur,

Let ΒΕ be greater. Extend it to Ζ, set ΕΖ equal to ΕΔ, and bisect ΒΖ at Η.

δίχα · in duas partes aequales — into two equal parts. The single adverb δίχα is expanded in the Latin. We bisect the whole ΒΖ, not the original side ΒΕ. Ε and Η are distinct cuts of the same line when the sides differ. Η is Greek eta: it is the centre label in this edition, not the English label H for the top of the semicircle.

Printed pages 160, 161.

5. Draw the semicircle and meet it

καὶ κέντρῳ τῷ Η, διαστήματι δὲ ἑνὶ τῶν ΗΒ, ΗΖ ἡμικύκλιον γεγράφθω τὸ ΒΘΖ, καὶ ἐκβεβλήσθω ἡ ΔΕ ἐπὶ τὸ Θ, καὶ ἐπεζεύχθω ἡ ΗΘ.

et centro Η radio autem alterutra rectarum ΗΒ, ΗΖ semicirculus describatur ΒΘΖ, et producatur ΔΕ ad Θ, et ducatur ΗΘ.

With centre Η and radius either ΗΒ or ΗΖ, draw the semicircle ΒΘΖ. Extend ΔΕ to Θ, and join ΗΘ.

κέντρῳ … διαστήματι — with centre … with radius. Both datives specify how to draw. ἑνὶ τῶν means ‘one of the’, because the two half-lengths are equal. ΔΕ continues through Ε into the semicircle. The rectangle supplies a right angle at Ε. The lengths and coordinate orientation shown here are modern choices.

Printed pages 160, 161.

6. The first account of one square

Ἐπεὶ οὖν εὐθεῖα ἡ ΒΖ τέτμηται εἰς μὲν ἴσα κατὰ τὸ Η, εἰς δὲ ἄνισα κατὰ τὸ Ε, τὸ ἄρα ὑπὸ τῶν ΒΕ, ΕΖ περιεχόμενον ὀρθογώνιον μετὰ τοῦ ἀπὸ τῆς ΕΗ τετραγώνου ἴσον ἐστὶ τῷ ἀπὸ τῆς ΗΖ τετραγώνῳ.

iam quoniam recta ΒΖ in partes aequales secta est in Η in inaequales autem in Ε, erunt ΒΕ × ΕΖ + ΕΗ² = ΗΖ².

Since ΒΖ has been cut into equal parts at Η and unequal parts at Ε, the rectangle contained by ΒΕ and ΕΖ, together with the square on ΕΗ, equals the square on ΗΖ.

μετὰ τοῦ … τετραγώνου — together with the square. μετά with the genitive adds a figure to the comparison. This is II.5, whose statement is available among the source pages. Heiberg compresses the Greek sentence into an equation in his Latin translation. The multiplication sign and squared notation belong to that nineteenth-century rendering; they are not printed in this Greek sentence.

Printed pages 160, 162, 161, 163.

7. Equal radii exchange the square

ἴση δὲ ἡ ΗΖ τῇ ΗΘ· τὸ ἄρα ὑπὸ τῶν ΒΕ, ΕΖ μετὰ τοῦ ἀπὸ τῆς ΗΕ ἴσον ἐστὶ τῷ ἀπὸ τῆς ΗΘ.

sed ΗΖ = ΗΘ. itaque ΒΕ × ΕΖ + ΗΕ² = ΗΘ².

But ΗΖ equals ΗΘ. So the rectangle contained by ΒΕ and ΕΖ, together with the square on ΗΕ, equals the square on ΗΘ.

τὸ ἀπὸ τῆς ΗΘ — the [square] on ΗΘ. The noun ‘square’ is understood after its earlier use. Both ΗΖ and ΗΘ run from the centre to the circle. Reversing ΕΗ to ΗΕ changes the order of the endpoints, not the segment or its square.

Printed pages 162, 163.

8. The second account of the same square

τῷ δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς ΗΘ ἴσα ἐστὶ τὰ ἀπὸ τῶν ΘΕ, ΕΗ τετράγωνα· τὸ ἄρα ὑπὸ τῶν ΒΕ, ΕΖ μετὰ τοῦ ἀπὸ ΗΕ ἴσα ἐστὶ τοῖς ἀπὸ τῶν ΘΕ, ΕΗ.

uerum ΘΕ² + ΕΗ² = ΗΘ². itaque ΒΕ × ΕΖ + ΗΕ² = ΘΕ² + ΕΗ².

The squares on ΘΕ and ΕΗ equal the square on ΗΘ. Therefore the rectangle contained by ΒΕ and ΕΖ, together with the square on ΗΕ, equals the squares on ΘΕ and ΕΗ.

τὰ … τετράγωνα — the squares, taken together. The plural names two squares whose combined area is compared with one. I.47 applies to the right triangle ΗΕΘ. It does not say that each of the smaller squares separately equals the square on the hypotenuse.

Printed pages 162, 163.

9. Remove what both sides have

κοινὸν ἀφῃρήσθω τὸ ἀπὸ τῆς ΗΕ τετράγωνον· λοιπὸν ἄρα τὸ ὑπὸ τῶν ΒΕ, ΕΖ περιεχόμενον ὀρθογώνιον ἴσον ἐστὶ τῷ ἀπὸ τῆς ΕΘ τετραγώνῳ.

subtrahatur, quod commune est, ΗΕ². itaque ΒΕ × ΕΖ = ΕΘ².

Let the common square on ΗΕ be subtracted. The remaining rectangle contained by ΒΕ and ΕΖ therefore equals the square on ΕΘ.

κοινὸν ἀφῃρήσθω — let the common part be subtracted. ἀφῃρήσθω is a third-person perfect passive imperative of ἀφαιρέω, ‘take away’. Latin subtrahatur is a passive subjunctive used as a command. The same area leaves both totals. This is an application of the common notion about subtracting equals from equals.

Printed pages 162, 163.

10. Return to the given figure

ἀλλὰ τὸ ὑπὸ τῶν ΒΕ, ΕΖ τὸ ΒΔ ἐστιν· ἴση γὰρ ἡ ΕΖ τῇ ΕΔ· τὸ ἄρα ΒΔ παραλληλόγραμμον ἴσον ἐστὶ τῷ ἀπὸ τῆς ΘΕ τετραγώνῳ. ἴσον δὲ τὸ ΒΔ τῷ Α εὐθυγράμμῳ. καὶ τὸ Α ἄρα εὐθύγραμμον ἴσον ἐστὶ τῷ ἀπὸ τῆς ΕΘ ἀναγραφησομένῳ τετραγώνῳ.

uerum ΒΕ × ΕΖ = ΒΔ; nam ΕΖ = ΕΔ. itaque ΒΔ = ΘΕ². sed ΒΔ = Α. itaque etiam figura rectilinea Α quadrato, quod in ΕΘ construi poterit, aequale est.

But the rectangle contained by ΒΕ and ΕΖ is ΒΔ, because ΕΖ equals ΕΔ. Thus ΒΔ equals the square on ΘΕ. And ΒΔ equals the rectilinear figure Α. So Α also equals the square that can be drawn on ΕΘ.

ἀναγραφησομένῳ — that will be drawn. This future passive participle agrees with τετραγώνῳ. The argument has found the side of the required square; actually drawing the square uses the earlier construction I.46. Latin ‘quod … construi poterit’ expresses what can be constructed. The final square on our plate makes this last operation visible.

Printed pages 162, 163.

11. The task has been accomplished

Τῷ ἄρα δοθέντι εὐθυγράμμῳ τῷ Α ἴσον τετράγωνον συνέσταται τὸ ἀπὸ τῆς ΕΘ ἀναγραφησόμενον· ὅπερ ἔδει ποιῆσαι.

Ergo datae figurae rectilineae Α aequale quadratum constructum est, id quod in ΕΘ describi poterit; quod oportebat fieri.

A square equal to the given rectilinear figure Α has therefore been constructed: the one that can be drawn on ΕΘ. This is what had to be done.

ὅπερ ἔδει ποιῆσαι — which is what had to be done. ποιῆσαι means ‘to do’ or ‘to make’. A construction ends with something made. A theorem commonly ends with δεῖξαι, ‘to show’. The opening infinitive συστήσασθαι sets the task; the perfect συνέσταται now presents the achieved result.

Printed pages 162, 163.

Source and model boundaries

J. L. Heiberg, Euclidis opera omnia, volume I, Leipzig: Teubner, 1883, pp. 160–163. Full pages 128–129 and 110–111 supply the statements of II.5 and I.47; their complete proofs are not transcribed. University of Toronto scan; public domain.

Line breaks, apparatus and inline Latin reference marks are omitted in the transcription. Greek ϑ becomes θ. Greek point labels remain Greek. Heiberg's Latin formulas, including his printed ‘aequale’ after ‘figura’ on p. 163, are retained. The full scans preserve the printed evidence.

For modern calculation, r = (a + b)/2, d = (a − b)/2 and h² = r² − d². Thus h² = ab. Chosen units, numerical approximations, algebraic vocabulary and the piece motion are teaching aids. The moving diagram is not a formal proof, an ancient measurement, a full implementation of I.45, or a construction for squaring a circle.

This file embeds its source scans and font, has no runtime scripts and makes no remote subresource requests. Its application link requires a connection. The completed rearrangement and the pre-subtraction account are retained for comparison, regardless of the captured view.
